pages.text: Start with an ordinary number. `2 × (2 + j1)` doubles both parts and makes `4 + j2`. Two copies of the arrow laid tip to tail land there, pointing the same way and twice as long.

pages.name: 3 × (2 − j1)
pages.why: Three lots of `2 − j1`. The real part is `3 × 2 = 6` and the `j` part is `3 × (−1) = −3`. The answer is `6 − j3`, the same arrow three times as long.

pages.alt: The complex plane, real across and j up. The arrow z runs from 0 to 2 plus j1. The answer lands on minus 1 plus j2. j times 2: j2. j times j1 equals j times j times 1: minus 1. Both lengths: the square root of (2 squared plus 1 squared): 2.24.

pages.text: Times `j` turns an arrow a quarter turn anticlockwise. Multiply out to see why. `j × (2 + j1) = j2 + j × j × 1`, and `j × j = −1`, so it makes `−1 + j2`.

pages.name: j × (3 + j1)
pages.why: `j × 3 = j3`, and `j × j1 = j × j × 1 = −1`. So `j × (3 + j1) = −1 + j3`, the arrow turned a quarter turn anticlockwise and just as long.

pages.name: Four tiles
pages.text: Two brackets multiply as the four tiles you met before, every part of the first times every part of the second. `(3 + j2)(1 + j2)` makes `3`, `j6`, `j2` and `j2 × j2 = j × j × 4`.

pages.name: (2 + j3)(1 − j2)
pages.why: The tiles are `2 × 1 = 2`, `2 × (−j2) = −j4`, `j3 × 1 = j3` and `j3 × (−j2) = −j × j × 6 = +6`. Real `2 + 6 = 8`, and the `j` parts `−4 + 3 = −1`. So the answer is `8 − j1`.

pages.alt: The complex plane, real across and j up. The arrow z runs from 0 to 2 plus j1, and jz, a quarter turn round, to minus 1 plus j2. The answer lands on 1 plus j3. Drag the tip of z, and move c and d.. Tiles for (2 plus j1)(1 plus j1): 2, j2, j1, j times j times 1. Real pile 1, j pile j3, so the answer is 1 plus j3.

pages.text: Split the second bracket. `z × (c + jd)` is `c` lots of `z` plus `d` lots of `jz`, and `jz` is `z` turned a quarter turn. Lay them tip to tail and they end on the answer.

pages.name: (1 + j2) × j2
pages.task: Work out `(1 + j2) × j2`. Here `c = 0` and `d = 2`.
pages.why: With `c = 0` and `d = 2` it is 2 lots of `jz`. `jz = j × (1 + j2) = −2 + j1`, so twice that is `−4 + j2`. The tiles agree, `1 × j2 = j2` and `j2 × j2 = j × j × 4 = −4`.

pages.alt: The complex plane, real across and j up. The arrow z runs from 0 to 2 plus j1. The answer lands on 1 plus j3. Length of 1 plus j1: the square root of 2: 1.41. Length of 2 plus j1: the square root of 5: 2.24. Length of 1 plus j3: the square root of 10: 3.16. 2.24 times 1.41: 3.16.

pages.text: Why a stretch and turn? `c` lots of `z` then `d` lots of `jz` make a right-angled corner, as `jz` is `z` turned a quarter. `c + jd` is the same corner drawn from 1, `c` across and `d` up. So the answer is that shape laid along `z` at `z`'s size, and whatever turn and stretch takes 1 to `c + jd` takes `z` to the answer.

pages.name: (4 + j2) × (−j1)
pages.why: `−j × 4 = −j4`, and `−j × j2 = −j × j × 2 = +2`. So the answer is `2 − j4`, the arrow turned a quarter turn clockwise and just as long.

pages.alt: The complex plane, real across and j up. The arrow z runs from 0 to 1 plus j1, and jz, a quarter turn round, to minus 1 plus j1. The answer lands on j2. Tiles for (1 plus j1) squared: 1, j1, j1, j times j times 1. Real pile 0, j pile j2, so the answer is j2.

pages.text: Squaring is multiplying a number by itself. `(1 + j1)²` has four tiles, `1`, `j1`, `j1` and `j1 × j1 = j × j × 1 = −1`. Real `1 − 1 = 0`, and the `j` parts `1 + 1 = 2`, so `(1 + j1)² = j2`.

pages.name: Double and turn
pages.task: Which number, multiplying any arrow, doubles it and turns it a quarter turn anticlockwise?
pages.why: Times 2 doubles an arrow, and times `j` turns it a quarter turn anticlockwise, so times `j2` does both. On `2 + j1`, `j2 × (2 + j1) = j4 + j × j × 2 = −2 + j4`, twice as long and turned a quarter turn.
